B) A WRIT ORDER OR DIRECTION IN NATURE OF CERTIORARI, BY QUASHING ANNEXURE-O, VIZ, THE FINAL NOTIFICATION DATED 20.12.2013 PUBLISHED BY THE RESPONDENT NO 1 IN THE GAZETTE U/SEC 3-D OF THE NATIONAL HIGHWAYS ACT,1956, IN SO FAR AS IT PERTAINS TO SY NO. 96 AND 96/B OF HANCHINAL VILLAGE AND ETC.,
THIS WRIT PETITION IS COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:

ORDER Heard Sri D.P. Ambekar, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri Sudhir Singh R.Vijapur, learned DSGI for respondent No.1, Sri Sachin Mahajan and Smt. Shilpa Shah, learned counsels for respondent Nos.2 and 3 and Smt. Maya T.R., learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.4.
2.

Writ petition is filed with the following prayer:
(a) Issue a writ, order or direction in nature of certiorari, by quashing Annexure-N,
viz, the NC: 2024:KHC-K:2260 impugned notification dated 17.06.2013 bearing No SO.1709(E), issued by the respondent No. 1, and all further proceedings on basis of the same.

sentences.text: 2 b) A writ order or direction in nature of certiorari, by quashing Annexure-O, viz, the final notification dated 20.12.2013 published by the respondent No.1 in the gazette u/sec 3-D of the National Highways Act,1956, in so far as it pertains to Sy No. 96 and 96/B of Hanchinal village.

c) Alternatively and without prejudice to the above prayers, a writ order or direction in nature of mandamus, directing the respondents to acquire only the area shown to be acquired from the said lands of the petitioner as is shown before the said lands from the NH-13, ie., an area of 1026 sq mts from 96/1A and an area of 618 sq mts from Sy.No.96/1B both of Hanchinal village, as measured from the NH-13.

d) Any type of writ or order or direction may be passed as deemed fit in the facts and circumstances of case in interest of justice and equity."
3.

Facts in brief which are utmost necessary for disposal of the writ petition are as under:
Land in Sy.Nos.96/1A and 96/B situated in Hanchinala village, were notified for acquisition by the National Highway NC: 2024:KHC-K:2260 Authority by exercising power under Section 3-D of the National Highways Act.
Final notification was also issued and compensation amount was deposited.
4. Petitioner has withdrawn the compensation amount under protest with liberty to challenge the very acquisition and therefore, filed the present writ petition.

5. Reiterating the grounds urged in the petition, Sri D.B. Ambekar, learned counsel for the petitioner contended that before passing the final notification, petitioner was not heard and there was no opportunity granted for the petitioner to oppose the intended acquisition and sought for allowing the writ petition.
6. In other words, petitioner submits that before final notification came to be passed under Annexure-O, principles of natural justice is not followed.
7. Per contra, Smt. Shilpa Shah, representing National Highways Authorities supported the final notification at Annexure-O and so also learned High Court Government Pleader.
8. Having heard the parties, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.
On such perusal, it is seen that petitioner is the only person who has opposed the formation of the National Highways.
The grounds on which the petitioner is challenging the acquisition would amount to interfering with the policy of the Central Government in forming the road.

sentences.text:
According to the petitioner, the very project itself is eccentric in nature and therefore, the objections of the petitioner ought to have been taken into consideration before the final notification came to be passed.
11.

Under Section 3-D of National Highways Authorities Act, it is the National Highway Authorities which is the proper person to recommend for formation of a highways which would be approved by the Central Government.
12. It is for the authorities to find out which is the land which is expedient to be acquired for the said purpose.
13. In the case on hand, none of the land losers have challenged the formation of the Highway.
Infact, formation of a highway is part of the developmental activities of a nation.
14. Further, it is settled principles of law that the private interest should yield to the public interest at large.
Therefore, the acquisition notification issued under Annexures- NC: 2024:KHC-K:2260 N and O are just and proper and suitable compensation has been awarded.
15. Infact, the petitioner has already withdrawn the compensation amount.
If the petitioner is of the opinion that the compensation amount is not adequate, the forum for the petitioner lies elsewhere.
16. With this observation, this Court is of the considered opinion that the grounds urged in the writ petition are hardly sufficient to quash the Annexures-N and O.

Hence, following:
ORDER Writ petition is dismissed.
No order as to costs.
